paragraphs: CourseLeaf sells an academic operations platform to colleges and universities, covering the work of publishing catalogs, moving curriculum through approvals, building class schedules and helping students register. It is sold as named modules for student registration, curriculum management, academic catalog, and academic scheduling and analytics.

The software is built to sit alongside a campus student information system, using a bi-directional integration and a validation step meant to keep data consistent across systems. It is aimed at the awkward cases institutions actually have, such as cross-listed courses, effective terms, reserved seats and learning outcomes mapping. The company says every deployment is tailored, counting more than 2,000 implementations that each included something built for that institution.

By its own count the software has helped over 550 campuses, from community colleges and small private institutions to state universities. The platform comes from Leepfrog Technologies. That company was launched in 1994 in Iowa City. It reports more than 140 team members. Most of them are in the Iowa City-Cedar Rapids region, home to the headquarters, while some work remotely.

quote.text: Software should adapt to the needs of the institution.
